newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Rafinerska hikes petrol price as crown drops.
newsitem.headline: Czech Rafinerska hikes petrol price as crown drops.

text.p: The main Czech crude oil refinery Ceska Rafinerska a.s. said on Wednesday its supplies of refined petrol would rise by 580 crowns per tonne as of June 1, in-part because of the sharp fall of the Czech crown.

In a statement, Rafinerska spokesman Ales Soukup, said the weakening of the crown, tempered by a lowering of crude prices on world markets, would cause the sale price for one litre of petrol in the Czech Republic to rise by 44 hellers (cents).
He declined to give the actual price charged to distributors, calling it a "trade secret".
The retail price in the Czech Republic for 95 octane lead-free petrol has averaged roughly 21 crowns per litre recently, with diesel at about 18 crowns per litre.
Soukup told Reuters that the price for motor diesel fuel would rise by 500 crowns per tonne, meaning a increase in the sale price of 42 hellers per litre.
Nearly all of the Czech Republic's crude oil supplies are imported and are sensitive to currency swings.
The Czech crown has fallen roughly eight percent against the dollar and seven percent against the mark since the Czech National Bank was forced to freely float the currency on Monday.
Ceska Rafinerska is 51 percent owned by the state controlled Unipetrol a.s., and 49 percent by the IOC consortium comprised of U.S. DuPont unit Conoco, Royal Dutch/Shell, and Italy's Agip.
